A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Diffusion Actor-Critic. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and corresponding material can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original D4RL evaluations, 2-D bandit experiments, and Q-guidance and value-target ablations in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds Adroit/Kitchen evaluations, parameter sensitivity experiments and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The soft Q-guidance loss, LCB critic ensemble, target-network updates, optional dual ascent and action-selection procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 explicitly lists additional existing inputs, and Appendix B.3 clarifies sample averaging without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 adds two Adroit datasets, pen-human-v1 and pen-cloned-v1, and three Kitchen datasets, complete/partial/mixed-v0. These introduce two additional evaluation domains beyond the retained locomotion, antmaze and bandit coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces TD3+BC and AWAC with DTQL and AlignIQL while retaining the other baselines. The Q-guidance comparison also drops its SOTA reference row when moving from v1 Table 5 to v2 Table 2. These are limited changes to the existing broad comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 introduces controlled sweeps of ensemble size, action-sample count, diffusion steps, behavior-cloning threshold and pessimism factor. Appendix C.4 adds single-batch-update timing comparisons at diffusion lengths 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100. The original two-million-step training budget and convergence-window scoring remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix C.3 substantially extend sensitivity analysis to five parameters, examining stability, convergence and dependence on sampling choices. The earlier guidance-type and LCB-versus-minimum ablations are retained; moving the latter to Appendix C.2 does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose eight independent training processes, ten evaluation seeds per process and 80 rollouts per evaluation in Appendix B. Both already report ± values and shaded training curves. v2 introduces no new uncertainty definition, repeated-run policy or significance test.

E6.justification: DAC's Table 1 scores are unchanged, but v2 adds comparator scores, Adroit/Kitchen outcomes and sensitivity/timing results. Table 5 reports DAC domain averages of 72.6 and 62.6; Table 8 reports soft-to-denoised guidance update-time ratios of 45.1% at T=5 and 5.4% at T=100. These are newly reported outcomes, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, Lemma 1, their Appendix A proofs and the underlying assumptions remain substantively unchanged. Policy notation gains an iteration index, and the generic Bellman-backup exposition is shortened without changing the retained LCB formulation.

C1.justification: v2 adds explicit training-efficiency claims to the contributions and conclusion, replacing v1's contribution-level emphasis on inference efficiency. The central KL-constrained diffusion-policy contribution remains unchanged. Convergence without early stopping was already claimed in v1, although v2 foregrounds it.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting ensemble size to smoother Q-gradient fields and small action batches to denoising randomness, plus parameter-specific convergence tradeoffs. Appendix C.1 qualifies comparisons with DQL because it uses online model selection. The antmaze reward-sparsity limitation remains, while the earlier critique of convex-combination value targets is omitted.

D1.justification: The original architecture, hardware, training-time estimate and default hyperparameters are retained, while new experiments disclose their tested parameter values and timing procedure. v2 removes the direct DAC repository link from v1's abstract and adds an explicit link to the cited JAXRL base; this changes access information without establishing that DAC code became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning through trust-region methods, DTQL and a new discussion of online diffusion RL, including QSM, DIPO and entropy-regulated diffusion actors. Additional ensemble-method citations also broaden the critic's research context beyond v1's narrower related-work treatment.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable. v2 edits the abstract and contributions, consolidates critic learning into Section 3.1, moves LCB discussion into the appendix and promotes Q-guidance scores into the main text. Citation style, author formatting and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a guidance schematic, sensitivity plots, Adroit/Kitchen training curves and new results/timing tables. Existing figures are reformatted or relocated, Table 1 changes columns, and the Q-guidance and LCB tables exchange main-text/appendix placement. The conference layout substantially changes display sizing and arrangement.

improvement.justification: The added domain evaluations, sensitivity studies and per-update timing measurements better support DAC's practical behavior and parameter choices. However, integration is incomplete: Section 5.1 retains the claim of over 10% gains on every medium task despite the newly added DTQL scores in Table 1, and the direct DAC code link disappears. The expanded evidence provides a net benefit, tempered by these reporting and access shortcomings.
